science.title: Dielectrophoresis-enhanced rejuvenation of water-tree-degraded XLPE cables under an AC electric field: a particle trajectory analysis
science.description: The study investigates the rejuvenation of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cables affected by water tree degradation using a combination of an applied AC voltage and the resulting dielectrophoretic force. The finite element method in COMSOL Multiphysics is implemented to show that the integrity of the cable is heavily compromised due to an intensified electric field around water trees. Two rejuvenation scenarios were examined: one with the cable de-energized, and the other with a fraction of its nominal voltage applied. In the meantime, the particle trajectory instrument is employed to analyze the motion of rejuvenation fluid in relation to both its development and accumulation within the water tree region. Dielectrophoretic forces cause the rejuvenation fluid to focus on the water tree region under an AC electric field. This leads to the idea that the application of controlled voltage during the rejuvenation process may enhance fluid penetration and has potential relevance to the reliability of XLPE cables.

science.title: A neuron's molecular clock: NMDA timing shapes the flow of information
science.description: In the brain, what matters is not only whether a signal reaches a nerve cell, but also how long its chemical gate remains open. A team led by Dr. Mehdi Borjkhani from the International Centre for Translational Eye Research (ICTER) has demonstrated in a computational model that both excessively fast and excessively slow NMDA-receptor deactivation can disrupt neuronal activity. Importantly, these extremes in cessation rates lead to instability through two distinct mechanisms.
